title: Accept a registered run's record after a benign same-holder claim recovery, so a lapse during a long run no longer loses it
outcome: Accept a registered run's record after a benign same-holder claim recovery, so a lapse during a long run no longer loses it
acceptance: A registered record whose run crosses the claim's original expiry is accepted when it is sent while the initiating session holds the claim again: after a same-holder renewal during the run, or after a same-holder recovery of the lapsed claim, even at a higher fence. It is refused for good on a takeover, handoff, release, closed ancestor or root change

If the claim is released, handed off or taken by another session after registration, the record is refused with field claim; while an ancestor of the work is closed, the record is refused with field claim (terminal for that record), whatever the request time

Behaviour tests send a registered record for a run that crosses the claim's original expiry and observe it acknowledged, both after a renewal during the run and after a same-holder recovery at a higher fence

Re-sent unchanged after the same session recovers its lapsed claim at a higher fence, with the claim's named root still bound under the registered generation (as when a restart has the host name the same path again), the record is accepted; a root that has since ended, been named again at a later generation, or been bound to another workspace refuses it with field root

While the initiating session's claim has lapsed but it can still claim the work again, or a handoff offer is open, the record is refused with the retryable field claim_live and nothing is stored, so the same key and body are accepted when sent again after recovery; a claim under a closed ancestor is refused with field claim
